relations.rationale: Rotating through stations to test circuits and calibrate sensors plausibly contributed to robots later moving without tipping, so it makes B somewhat more likely.
Calibrating sensors during the morning supports the later claim that some robots used sensors to avoid obstacles.
Rosa and Quinn working different shifts is unrelated to mentors circulating to offer tips.
Rosa and Quinn working different shifts does not determine whether Ben and Quinn worked different shifts.
Rosa and Quinn working different shifts is consistent with and slightly supports the existence of multiple shifts, hinting at least two shifts, though not specifically three.
Rosa and Quinn's shift schedule has no bearing on whether teams promised to bring improved designs.
Uma being younger than Gus does not determine her age relative to Ben.
Uma's age relative to Gus has no bearing on whether worktables were labeled with numbers.
Uma's age relative to Ben is unrelated to the robots' ability to move without tipping.
Mentors offering tips on wiring and balance plausibly helped the robots achieve stable movement by day's end.
Mentors' tips focused on wiring and balance, not sensors, so this has little direct bearing on obstacle avoidance via sensors.
Ben and Quinn working different shifts is consistent with there being multiple shifts, providing weak support for three shifts existing.
Ben and Quinn's shift assignment has no bearing on whether Uma brought the first-aid kit.
Labeling worktables with numbers is unrelated to the number of shifts the shop ran.
Labeling worktables to prevent mixed materials is unrelated to robots avoiding obstacles using sensors.
Robots being able to move without tipping is a prerequisite for some of them also avoiding obstacles, so it supports that claim.
Robots achieving stable movement by day's end could encourage teams to want to improve further, weakly supporting promises of better designs.
Some robots successfully avoiding obstacles could motivate other teams to promise improved designs, offering weak support.
Comparing notes about battery performance is a plausible precursor to teams promising improved designs, giving some support.
